header.running_head: Being Particular About Ta'leem (Learning and teaching) when in Jihaad in the path of Allaah

blocks.arabic_text: وَمَا كَانَ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ لِيَنْفِرُوا كَافَّةً فَلَوْلَا نَفَرَ مِنْ كُلِّ فِرْقَةٍ مِّنْهُمْ طَائِفَةٌ لِّيَتَفَقَّهُوا فِي الدِّينِ وَلِيُنْذِرُوا قَوْمَهُمْ إِذَا رَجَعُوا إِلَيْهِمْ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَحْذَرُونَ
blocks.text: It is not (correct) for the Mu'mineen to proceed (in Jihaad) all together (simultaneously when it is not Fardh for all to participate).

Then was the practice that while a party of Muslims would march with Rasulullaah ﷺ, another party would remain behind. Those that remained behind with Rasulullaah ﷺ would attain a deep understanding of Deen so that they may warn their people (those who had been engaged in Jihaad) when they return to them from the expeditions. In this manner, they were aware of what Allaah revealed in the Qur'aan, about their obligations and about the limits that Allaah had set."[^1]
The Letter of Hadhrat Umar (RA) to his Commanders about Attaining a Deep Understanding of Deen

Hadhrat Ahwas bin Hakeem bin Umayr Absi narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) wrote the following in a letter addressed to the commanders of the various Muslims armies, "Endeavour to attain a deep understanding of Deen because no person can be excused for pursuing falsehood thinking that it is the truth. Similarly, no one can be excused for forsaking the truth in the belief that it is falsehood."[^2]
The Sahabah (RA) sit in Gatherings (To Learn and Teach) while on Journey

Hadhrat Hitaan bin Abdullaah Raqaashi narrates that they were once part of an army under the command of Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA). They were travelling along the banks of the Tigris River when the time for salaah arrived. After someone had called out the Adhaan for the Zuhr salaah, the people started making wudhu and Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA) also made wudhu. He then led them in salaah, after which they all sat in groups. When the time for the Asr salaah arrived, someone called out the Adhaan for Asr and the people again stood up to make wudhu. Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA) then instructed the Mu'adhin to announce, "Take note that none should make wudhu besides those whose wudhu had broken." Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA) then said, "It seems imminent that knowledge shall disappear and ignorance will prosper to the extent that because of ignorance, a man will use his sword to kill his own mother."[^3]
Aadam bin Abi Ayaas in his Ilm, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.5 Pg.228).
Abdur Razaaq, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.5 Pg.114) and Tahaawi in his Sharhu Ma'aanil Aathaar (Vol.1 Pg.27).
